text:
**Short answer:** For a typical full-size fridge, get a power station with about 1,500-2,000 Wh of capacity and a surge rating of at least 1,300 W (2,000 W+ is safer). That covers roughly a day. Around 1,000 Wh covers about 12-17 hours.

## What to check

1. **Surge watts (the most common failure).** The compressor briefly draws 2-3x its running power at startup. Sources put this at about 1,000-1,800 W for typical fridges and up to 2,400 W for large or older ones. A station with plenty of battery can still trip at startup if its surge rating is too low ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
2. **Continuous watts.** A fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station clears this. Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.
3. **Pure sine wave output.** This is preferred for compressor motors, and the reputable units below all have it.
4. **Watt-hours.** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. That's about 1,000-1,400 Wh per day after inverter losses and headroom. Use this rule of thumb:
   - About 1,000 Wh: roughly 17 hours
   - About 1,400-2,000 Wh: roughly 1 day
   - About 2,800 Wh or more: roughly 2 days

   Sources: [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator).

**To fit your own fridge:** find the kWh/year on its EnergyGuide label. Then compute kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 for average watts. Multiply by 24 hours, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average twice the typical figure, so size up for those. Keeping the door shut stretches runtime.

## Options that fit

- **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W surge): good for about half a day to a day. It was $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF according to Dealectric's cart test on 2026-10-21.
- **[ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh)** (1,451 Wh, 2,400 W, 4,000 W surge): about a day. It was $664 with code ALLPOWERS26 (tested 2026-10-25).
- **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)** (2,073 Wh): about 33 hours under HomeGridHQ's conservative assumptions. It was $899 with code AFF5OFF (tested 2026-10-25).
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)** (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak): a 2 kWh-class option for longer backup. That link is Anker's guide page, not a direct product listing.

The Dealectric links are affiliate links, so it earns a commission. Prices and codes change, so confirm at checkout. Runtimes are estimates, and heat, door openings and an older fridge will shorten them.

If you tell me your fridge's EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one model.
